digest.component_or_area: plan-review severity model / impact-model hard-override axes
propositions: The undecomposed axis fires on 0.107–0.153% of verified findings (11/10,250 plan-v3, 18/11,773 plan-v4), two orders of magnitude below every other severity axis, yet holds sole hard-override power flooring impact to 0.85.

The stated rationale—that a deterministic G5 suppressor prevents false fires on childless tickets—is factually inert: the suppressor fired zero times across 2,000 reviews and cannot apply to 90%+ of the childless-ticket population.

The grade-to-floor mapping is miscalibrated: 16 of 29 fires carry low grade, and in 25 of 29 cases the 0.85 floor was the only override present, making low grades block decisions solely via the floor rather than proportional severity.

The inverse population (findings text-matching the flat-plan regex but scoring undecomposed=none) contains no missed genuine defects; regex matches are false positives on code/module decomposition unrelated to plan structure.
All 29 firing findings are genuine flat-plan or bundled-work defects; 6 blocked and 23 were advisory or dropped, confirming the axis detects real problems but at miscalibrated impact weight.
